_readme: Lisa's OWN reviewed snapshot of what this repository's merge rules require, and of what each `skip_jobs` token would silence. `scripts/check-skipped-required-checks.mjs` (here: `typescript/copy-overwrite/scripts/…`) makes the two police each other.

This file did not exist until #2933. Without it the `🔒 Skipped Required Checks` job printed `skipping` and reported SUCCESS on every pull request since it shipped — the guard against silencing required checks was itself silently green, on the repository that owns the epic against exactly that.

`required_contexts` was transcribed live on `baseline_fetched_at` from the two branch rulesets named in `ruleset.ids`, byte for byte, emoji and the ' / ' separator included. Reproduce it with: gh api repos/CodySwannGT/lisa/rulesets/ID --jq '.rules[] | select(.type=="required_status_checks") | .parameters.required_status_checks[].context'
Both rulesets carry the same ref condition (~DEFAULT_BRANCH plus refs/heads/dev, refs/heads/staging, refs/heads/main), so the list is the union of the two rather than a per-branch selection.
`skip_job_declarations` is EMPTY because `.github/workflows/ci.yml` passes `skip_jobs: ''` — this repository skips nothing. An entry is only ever needed for a token this repository really writes.

`enforcement` is deliberately ABSENT, which means BLOCK. The seeds Lisa ships set it to `warn` so a fresh install does not go red on arrival; this snapshot has been transcribed, so the ramp does not apply.

The transcription expires after 90 days, because a ruleset is edited in an admin console with no signal in this repository. When it expires this job goes red saying NOT CHECKED — that is the design: re-run the `gh api` line above, paste the result, and move the date.

`evidence_bearing_checks` names the checks whose GREEN is supposed to mean something reviewed the code. `.github/workflows/review-evidence.yml` runs the vacuity arm against every pull request here; before #2928 nothing invoked it at all, and of the last 25 merged pull requests 23 carried a REQUIRED `CodeRabbit` context reporting `success` with a description that says it did no work (9 `Review rate limited`, 14 `Review skipped: manual review required for this OSS repository`, 2 `Review completed`). That workflow is REPORT-ONLY on purpose and can still go red for one reason that is not a finding: it inspected NOTHING. Read the `vacuity_*` token before calling a red run a hollow review.
